title: Gate @objectstack/spec range floors against the symbols each package publishes
body:
Fixes #5793

A package's declared `@objectstack/spec` floor must carry every symbol that package's own build output references. It did not, and nothing could tell.

`@object-ui/plugin-detail` ships `dist/renderers/record-reference-rail.d.ts` containing `export type { ReferenceRailEntry } from '@objectstack/spec/ui'`, while its `dependencies` named a floor a minor lower than the spec that first exports that symbol. A declared range is a public claim: any consumer resolution landing the older spec satisfied it and got a dangling type re-export. Normal installs resolve the newest 17.x and never see it, which is exactly why nothing found it — it is a floor-honesty defect, and the lockfile hides it from every other check in this repository.

Direction is the triage ruling on the card: **floors track reality**. No argument that the uniform floor is deliberate is made here; that would be a maintainer ruling.

## Two deliverables

**1. The gate — `scripts/check-spec-range-floors.mjs` (`pnpm check:spec-floors`).** For every published package declaring the spec in a consumer-facing field, it compares that package's `dist` imports of `@objectstack/spec/*` against the export set of the version its own range admits at its lowest, and fails naming the symbol.

**2. The one measured bump.** `@object-ui/plugin-detail` → `^17.1.0`. It is the only range this PR changes, and the gate names the symbol behind it. The gate finds nothing else to justify one across the 19 packages in the population.

## The population was re-derived, not taken from the card

`packages/providers` is **not** in it: PR #6048 removed its `@objectstack/spec` edge entirely. On `a1c41c516` the population is **19** published packages declaring the spec in `dependencies` / `peerDependencies` / `optionalDependencies` — one smaller than the card's table. Eight more declare it only in `devDependencies`, which floors nobody; an artifact importing a dev-only dependency is a phantom dependency and stays `check-phantom-dependencies.mjs`'s finding.

## The two hazards that produce a confident green

Both are avoided by construction, not by care, and the header of the gate carries the long version.

**Root hoisting makes resolution answer the wrong question.** The root `package.json` declares `@objectstack/spec`, so pnpm hoists it and `require.resolve` succeeds from any package regardless of that package's own manifest. **A green type-check therefore proves nothing about a floor and is not cited as evidence anywhere in this PR** — it type-checks against the installed 17.2.0. The gate resolves nothing through `node_modules`: it fetches the declared minimum from the registry and reads that tarball's own manifest. A test asserts the source contains no `createRequire` / `require.resolve` / `import.meta.resolve` (comments stripped first, since the header names them to explain the trap).

**The spec is dual-package.** The gate walks the *fetched* manifest's `exports` map under the `import` condition and **prints the entry it landed on**, e.g.

```
@objectstack/spec@17.0.0 "./ui"  [import > types]  ./dist/ui/index.d.mts
@objectstack/spec@17.1.0 "./ui"  [import > types]  ./dist/ui/index.d.mts
```

That is the **ESM types entry** (`.d.mts`), not the `require` half. `--cross-check` re-reads the `require` half and compares: **45 entry points compared, the two halves export the same names.** They agree today — a measurement, not a licence to read whichever is convenient, which is why the comparison is executable rather than a claim.

## Non-vacuity — three executable controls

| Control | Result |
|---|---|
| Floor too low | **red**, naming the symbol: `packages/plugin-detail/dist/renderers/record-reference-rail.d.ts references ReferenceRailEntry from @objectstack/spec/ui, which @objectstack/spec@17.0.0 does not export`; and it names the answer: `@object-ui/plugin-detail → "@objectstack/spec": "^17.1.0"` |
| After the bump | **green** (exit 0), the run consulting 17.1.0 for `./ui` and `./data` on that package and 17.0.0 for the rest — so the floor is read per package, not globally |
| Floor deliberately lowered again | **red** again, same symbol |

A fourth control was run to prove the gate is not wired to one package and one symbol: lowering `@object-ui/core` to a genuinely older major reds it with **five different real symbols across two subpaths, from both `.d.ts` and `.js` artifacts** — `CONTEXT_TOKENS`, `isRuntimeDefaultToken`, `PercentScale`, `SEARCH_VIRTUAL_TYPES` (`/data`), `DATE_RANGE_PRESETS` (`/ui`) — and honestly reports that **no** published version of that major would satisfy it, rather than inventing a bump.

Every mutation ran under a restoring `trap`, and each one was **proved on disk** before its reading was taken (anchor count before/after plus injected count); the tree was verified byte-identical afterwards.

## Why `dist` and not `src`, and why this is not a per-PR gate

`src` is cheaper and wrong in the direction that costs most here: an `import type` used only inside a function body is erased and never reaches `dist`, so a source-level gate would demand floor bumps nothing published justifies — corrupting exactly the rule that every range changed must be backed by a symbol the gate names.

That makes this the repository's second artifact-level gate, so it is wired the way the first one is: the **publish path** (`pnpm changeset:publish`, where a lying floor cancels the release) plus a **nightly alarm**, and **no `pull_request` trigger** — the 2026-08-16 ruling on #4846 rejected a per-PR full-repo build and nothing here reopens it. A test fails if this gate is ever added to a workflow carrying that trigger.

## The exclusion that could have made it blind

Symbol names are read from type declarations and ES modules. The minified UMD/CJS bundle is not parsed for names — its externals are property accesses on a factory parameter, so no name survives. That exclusion is **guarded, not trusted**: every spec subpath a bundle names as a string literal must also be covered by a readable artifact, or it is an `opaque-subpath` finding.

The first spelling of that guard scanned raw **text** and produced **30 findings across 15 packages on its first run — every one a doc comment** (`@objectstack/spec/ui.` with the sentence's full stop attached, `@objectstack/spec/data/object.zod.ts` naming a source file, `@objectstack/spec/view` naming an entry point that does not exist). Scanning string literals instead drops all 30 and keeps the real question. A test pins that prose case with those exact strings.

## Verification

Union re-run on the final commit **`e3f610f9a`**:

- `check:spec-floors --cross-check` **exit 0** — `Every consumer-facing @objectstack/spec floor carries the symbols its package's artifact references.` over 19 of 39 published packages, 2024 artifact files, 262 (subpath, symbol) pairs judged
- `check:control-bytes`, `check:phantom-deps`, `check:self-import`, `changeset-fixed`, `changeset-no-major`, `changeset-presence`, `lint-coverage`, `type-check-coverage`, `type-check:scripts`, `lint:root`, `doc-links`, `doc-component-types` — **all exit 0** (each exit code captured before any pipe)
- `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/__tests__/ packages/plugin-detail/` from the **repo root** — **166 files, 2739 tests, 0 failures**
- `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/plugin-detail' type-check` — exit 0

**Lint narrowing, declared.** `pnpm lint:root` (the root ESLint project, which owns `scripts/` and `.github/`) ran in full and is green — 0 errors, 26 pre-existing warnings that `lint.yml`'s header records as known debt. The two new files were additionally linted directly with `--no-inline-config --format json`: **2 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings**. `eslint.config.js` enables **no type-aware linting** (no `projectService`, no `parserOptions.project`), so this diff cannot move the verdict on any file it does not touch. The full per-package `pnpm lint` farm is CI's run.

**The gate's own tests are non-vacuous.** A five-mutation battery was run against `scripts/__tests__/check-spec-range-floors.test.ts`. Four were caught immediately; **one survived** — replacing the "this range names no lower bound" throw with a permissive `'0.0.0'`, i.e. the single most important safety property of the gate. Every range in the test set was rejected while parsing a comparator, so none ever reached that branch. A range that caps without flooring is the one spelling that gets there; those cases were added, and the mutation is now caught. The battery is recorded here rather than in the tree.

## Changeset

`patch` for `@object-ui/plugin-detail`. `check-changeset-presence.mjs` reports none owed — it watches `src/` of released packages, and this changes a manifest — but a dependency floor is part of what consumers install, and #5753's changeset is the in-repo precedent for scoring a dependency-field-only change on a released package as `patch` ("the change is to the install graph only"). Not `minor`: the lockfile still resolves 17.2.0 on this edge after the bump, so nothing a consumer installs today changes. Never `major`.

## Also touched

`content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md` — a new workflow needs a section and an inventory row there, enforced by `scripts/__tests__/ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts`. Its sibling ratchet then correctly caught a frozen version literal in my first draft of that prose; the literal was removed and the page points at `packages/plugin-detail/package.json` instead.

Out of scope, untouched: any range the gate does not justify, the spec package itself, and `packages/providers`.
